title: VLOOKUP: approximate match needs a sorted column

screens.prompt: In B6, look up the commission rate for the revenue in A6 across the bands in A2:B5, using approximate match.

hints.syntax: =VLOOKUP(A6,A2:B5,2,TRUE), with the last argument written rather than left out.
hints.func-vlookup: VLOOKUP is what the screen tests, so no INDEX and MATCH substitution, even where it would answer correctly.
hints.match-type: TRUE as the fourth argument. The band table needs an approximate match, and 1 means the same to Excel.
hints.require-ref: Read the revenue from A6. Type 4200 into the formula and the rate stops following the sheet.
hints.value: Which band covers 4200? The one that starts at 1000, so the rate is column 2 of A2:B5. Column 1 would hand back 1000.
hints.error: A2:B5 is two columns wide, so the third argument can only be 1 or 2. Anything wider stops at #REF!.

reject.why: no fourth argument means approximate match, but the exercise wants it written
exact match returns #N/A because no band starts at 4200
right answer written with a different function
the revenue is typed in, so the answer never follows A6
a text column index stops the formula with #VALUE!

screens.prompt: These bands are out of order, so which cell holds the rate that 4200 needs?
screens.alt: A commission band table with Revenue in column A and Rate in column B. Rows 2 to 5 read 0, 5000, 1000, 10000 with rates 2%, 8%, 5%, 10%. Cell A7 holds 4200 and B7 is empty; the formula bar reads =VLOOKUP(A7,A2:B5,2,TRUE).

hints.value: Approximate match needs a column that rises, and this one does not. The 1000 band sits on row 4 under 5000, so read B4, the rate, rather than the band beside it.

docs.explain:
Approximate match walks the first column until the lookup value would pass, then steps back to the row it last cleared. That is why the bands rise: 4200 sits above the 1000 band in A3 and below 5000 in A4, so the formula returns the rate on the 1000 row, 0.05.

The fourth argument picks the mode. FALSE demands a band that starts at exactly 4200, and none does, so exact match answers #N/A. TRUE asks for the band below, and 1 means the same thing. The grader wants that argument written rather than implied.

A band table is only as good as its sort. Move 1000 under 5000 and the same formula stops on the wrong row.

errors.text: The lookup value is below the first band, and VLOOKUP has no earlier row to step back to.
The column index is text rather than a number, which names no column to read.
The column index points past the right edge of A2:B5, which holds two columns.

docs.atWork: Commission tiers, postage bands and tax brackets: tables written to be read approximately.
docs.outcome: Read a rate off a band table with approximate match, on a column that rises.

seo.title: VLOOKUP approximate match in Excel: bands
seo.description: Approximate match reads the band below the value, so a sorted first column is the whole contract. 4200 falls in the 1000 band, and the rate is 0.05.
